questions.q: What does a stateful firewall track in its state table?
options: Only the physical MAC addresses of connected devices
Which connections are currently open and what reply traffic to expect back
A list of every username that has ever logged into the network
Nothing — stateful firewalls do not maintain any ongoing records
questions.explain: The state table is the stateful firewall's running record of active connections, used to recognize and auto-allow legitimate replies.

questions.q: Why does a stateless firewall need an explicit rule to let reply traffic back in?
options: Stateless firewalls only process outbound traffic
Stateless firewalls block all reply traffic permanently by design
Reply traffic is always encrypted and cannot be filtered
It has no memory of prior traffic and evaluates every packet in isolation
questions.explain: With no state table, a stateless firewall can't recognize a reply as part of an approved conversation — it needs a static rule written for it.

questions.q: What is the real tradeoff between stateful and stateless firewalls described in this lesson?
options: There is no meaningful difference in cost or intelligence between them
Stateful firewalls cannot process encrypted traffic at all
Stateless firewalls are always more secure than stateful ones
Stateful is smarter but more resource-intensive; stateless is cheaper and faster but less intelligent
questions.explain: Tracking a state table costs CPU and memory; stateless filtering skips that cost but loses the ability to reason about connections.

questions.q: In the lesson's example, why does the stateful firewall allow the reply from 203.0.113.10:443 without a separate inbound rule?
options: The firewall allows all traffic from any address ending in .10
HTTPS traffic bypasses firewall inspection entirely
It matches an entry already in the state table for a connection the laptop initiated
Port 443 is always allowed inbound on every firewall by default
questions.explain: Because the laptop's outbound connection was already logged in the state table, the matching reply is recognized and passed automatically.

questions.q: Where does stateless packet filtering still commonly earn its place today?
options: Only inside next-generation firewalls, never on its own
On resource-constrained devices or as a fast first filtering pass before a stateful device
It no longer has any practical use anywhere
As the primary firewall technology in nearly all modern enterprise networks
questions.explain: Most modern firewalls are stateful by default, but stateless filtering still fits lightweight devices and quick pre-filtering roles.
